thesis: Figure runs a blockchain-native capital marketplace for consumer credit: partners originate on its loan origination system and sell loans through Figure Connect, a tokenized marketplace that reached 65% of Q2 2026 volume. Operating momentum is exceptional — Q2 2026 Consumer Loan Marketplace volume of $4.3B (+132% y/y), adjusted net revenue of $218M (+95%), GAAP net income of $87M and a 54.6% adjusted EBITDA margin — yet the stock is down ~62% from its January 2026 high of $78 after a short-seller report questioned the technology positioning and business model. At ~24x consensus FY2026 EPS of ~$1.20 and ~18x FY2027 ~$1.61, with the $590M Kiavi acquisition closed on 2026-09-01 adding a guided ~$100M of annual EBITDA, the setup is asymmetric but the credibility overhang, HELOC concentration and structural take-rate compression keep this speculative.

financials.fcf: N/A — operating cash flow distorted by loans held for sale ($597M at 2026-06-30)

drivers: Consumer Loan Marketplace volume compounds past a $20B annual run rate as the partner network grows beyond the 489 active partners reported for Q2 2026
Figure Connect mix moves toward management's revised ~70% medium-term expectation, lifting fee-based ecosystem revenue and pushing adjusted EBITDA margin to the 60%+ medium-term target
Kiavi delivers the guided ~$100M of annual EBITDA and ~40% volume uplift, and its residential transition loan technology becomes a standard private-label offering
Democratized Prime third-party assets keep compounding from ~$170M (2026-08-06) as originators replace traditional warehouse lines, adding a second capital-light revenue engine
Short-seller allegations fail to dent reported results and the multiple re-rates toward the $52.88 consensus target

base_case.assumptions: Q3 2026 volume lands in the guided $4.8B–$5.2B range and volume growth decelerates from triple digits toward 50–70% through 2027; net take rate holds at the low end of the 3.5%–4.0% band as Connect mix rises; Kiavi is integrated without material surprises; FY2027 EPS approximates the ~$1.61 consensus and the stock re-rates to roughly 25–28x, partially closing the gap to the $52.88 consensus target.

risks: Short-seller allegations gain traction or internal-control weaknesses resurface, forcing a lasting credibility discount on a blockchain-dependent narrative
HELOC demand rolls over with housing values or rates, exposing concentration in a single core product
Take rate compresses below 3.5% as the largest partners hit top volume tiers and first-lien mix grows, so revenue grows materially slower than volume
Credit normalisation raises delinquencies, widens securitization spreads from the ~135bps AAA level and impairs gain-on-sale economics
Kiavi integration disappoints while the $600M of 8.5% senior notes raised in July 2026 weighs on earnings

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results — confirmation of the $4.8B–$5.2B volume guide, first Kiavi contribution, and the promised new contribution-margin / unit-economics disclosure
First full quarter of Kiavi ownership after the 2026-09-01 close; management guided to ~$100M annual EBITDA and ~40% incremental volume
Democratized Prime expansion — long-term takeout via whole-loan sales and securitization of non-Figure assets, plus scaling of the SMB pools launched in July 2026
FY2026 results and expiry of the $200M share repurchase authorization on 2027-02-27; pace of buybacks at depressed prices is a signal on capital allocation
Federal Reserve rate path — rising rates hurt gain on sale and take rate, but also push consumers to tap home equity to refinance costlier debt
Regulatory treatment of tokenized real-world assets, the $YLDS registered yield-bearing stablecoin, DART and the OPEN blockchain share class

key_risks: Credibility overhang from the 2026 short-seller report questioning Figure's technology positioning and business model; hedge fund holders fell from 51 to 32 over Q2 2026
HELOC concentration — the company's own filings flag reliance on HELOCs and exposure to the HELOC market and housing values
Structural take-rate compression: Figure Connect carries the lowest take rate of the three channels and reached 65% of volume, with management guiding to the low end of the 3.5%–4.0% range
Consumer credit cycle: delinquencies, securitization spreads and whole-loan demand all deteriorate together in a downturn
Integration and leverage risk from the Kiavi acquisition, funded with $600M of unsecured senior notes at 8.5%
Dual-class structure with concentrated voting control (37.9M Class B shares) plus previously identified material weaknesses in internal controls still being remediated
Digital-asset regulatory uncertainty across $YLDS, DART, Democratized Prime and the OPEN share class
Persistent insider selling — 67,650 shares worth ~$2.16M sold in the three months to late September 2026 under 10b5-1 plans
